accuracy.evidence: Checked against the NHS and British Heart Foundation pages: the heart is a muscle about the size of a fist, in the chest slightly to the left, pumping blood through arteries (away) and veins (back); blood is always red. Lab paces (13, 16 and 28 beats per 10 s = 78, 96 and 168 bpm for sleep, sitting, running) sit inside the published child ranges (about 70-120 at rest for ages 6-7, higher in exercise, lower in sleep) and are labelled 'about'.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS1/KS2 heart misconceptions: the heart stops or rests at night (sleep step prediction and 'stop' feedback), blood only reaches the chest (tube step prediction 'Does blood go to your toes?'), heart is a bag of air or a bone, pulse can be felt anywhere (elbow/knee/hair taps get named feedback), and running slows the heart. Returning blood is drawn darker red, not blue, and the adult text names the blue-blood myth.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagheart is a pump-and-tubes model of circulation: squeezing pushes blood dots out along one vessel and back along another, joining a vessel to a body part is what lets blood reach it, pulse points are tested by tapping the body map, and activity changes the beat rate. Nothing in it is reusable for another topic by relabelling; flagbody (naming parts) and bodylab only label organs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Step 2 starts with no vessels, so squeezing does nothing until the child joins tubes, which shows why vessels are needed; the pulse step makes the child find which spots carry a beat; sit vs run and the sleep sandbox let the child discover the rate changes but never stops before the done message confirms it.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'helps you think', 'no, only the chest', 'elbow', 'slower' after a run, and 'stops' when asleep. Each is locked in before the task and revealed in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() gives a specific reply for each slip: brain vs heart (think), tummy vs heart (food), bones/muscles vs vessels, no pulse at elbow/hair with where to try instead, slower vs faster, heart never stops, sleep is slowest, lungs hold air, and blood reaches the toes all the time.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and everyday words (squeeze, tubes, tap tap tap), FK grade 0.4 against the family kid limit of 5.0; adult text FK 8.8 against 10.0. Curriculum terms used exactly: heart, muscle, pump, blood vessels, heartbeat, pulse, circulatory system (adult).

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases (the content gate passes); every kid paragraph states one fact or one thing to try, and each adult paragraph is curriculum link, vocabulary with numbers, named mistakes, or what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: The 'young' class gives 56 px buttons; the body map scales to the canvas (tall ratio 1.05 on phones) with tap radii of 34 px for parts and the heart; the walkthrough passes on iPhone 13 with every task completed and the status line kept below the feet.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a button twin (Squeeze the heart, Tube to head/arm/leg/tummy, Feel chest/wrist/neck/elbow/knee/hair, Sleep/Sit/Run); the canvas aria-label is updated with each action; the beat interval is skipped under reduced motion; axe is clean in both themes in the walkthrough.
